ruled: 2026-09-27, PROMPT-84 step 1b, by the platform owner
purpose: The house translation glossary, kept as DATA so one list feeds the lint, the pipeline gate and the bulk remediation. A term written into three scripts diverges; a term written once cannot.
how_scope_works: `scope` is a list of certification codes, or "*" for every certification. A term is only checked where it applies: `provider` means something specific under the EU AI Act and nothing in a Scrum item, and a word list applied outside its subject refuses correct work -- which is exactly how the superseded-Scrum-wording list came to refuse two ISO/IEC 42001 items for `development-team`.

severities.failure: A forbidden variant. Blocks a new row in the pipeline gate.
severities.flag: Reported for a human. Never blocks.

eu_ai_act.note: Roles under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. The Spanish forms are the official ES edition's; the Portuguese are the house forms ruled on 2026-09-27. The official PT edition of the Regulation IS held (sources/incoming/OJ_L_202401689_PT_TXT.pdf) and is the reference if these are ever disputed.

terms.note: The Spanish form collides with the vendor sense. Where a row means the COMMERCIAL VENDOR rather than the Regulation's role, Spanish uses `suministrador` -- see the vendor entry.
terms.autofix_note: NEITHER LANGUAGE IS AUTO-FIXABLE. `proveedor` is correct for the Regulation's role in Spanish, and `fornecedor` is the ordinary Portuguese word for a commercial vendor or supplier -- `fornecedor de dados`, `o fornecedor do modelo`. Exactly the sense collision the Spanish side already had, mirrored. A bulk substitution may run only over a read sample that establishes the role sense dominates, with the non-role members excluded by id.

terms.note: Bare `deployer` left in Portuguese is forbidden: it is a defined role in the Regulation and has an official rendering.
terms.autofix_note: The article is untouched: `o implantador` -> `o responsável pela implantação` and `do implantador` -> `do responsável pela implantação`, because `responsável` takes the same masculine article. Only NUMBER moves, which is why the plural has its own target rather than being derived. Bare `deployer` is fixable only in rows about the Regulation, which the regulation scope already enforces.

terms.note: THE ONE PLACE THE TWO LANGUAGES DIVERGE ON PURPOSE. Spanish needs `suministrador` for the vendor because `proveedor` is the Regulation's provider role. Portuguese has the opposite problem: `prestador` is the role, so `fornecedor` is free for the vendor. A row using `proveedor` for a vendor is not mechanically distinguishable from one using it for the role, so this is a FLAG for a human and never an auto-substitution.
terms.autofix_note: SENSE-DEPENDENT in both directions. Flag only.

terms.note: `alto risco` is ordinary Portuguese and reads correctly; the official rendering is `risco elevado`. Flagged rather than failed because the mixed corpus predates the ruling.
terms.autofix_note: OFF, and the contradiction is the reason rather than a preference. This term is severity `flag`: `alto risco` is ordinary Portuguese and was ruled a flag deliberately, so it never lands in FORBIDDEN and an autofix for it could never fire. A flag-severity term with autofix true is a contradiction in the data, and pin-glossary-autofix refuses to run rather than quietly skipping it.

terms.es: Reglamento de IA de la UE
terms.note: The Act's name is not left in English in either language.
terms.autofix_note: The Act has one name per language.

es.EU AI Act: Reglamento de IA de la UE
es.AI Act: Reglamento de IA de la UE

terms.note: `provedor` IS correct Portuguese in senses this catalogue uses -- `provedor de nuvem` is a cloud provider, not the Regulation's role. More importantly the ABNT edition of ISO/IEC 42001 and 22989 may render the 22989 role as `provedor de IA`, and we do not hold that edition, so the house form cannot be asserted there. It is therefore a FLAG everywhere and is NOT GATED AT ALL in AIMS-F or AIMS-IA until the ABNT term is known. Separated from the `fornecedor` entry because the two have different severities and different reasons, and one entry carrying both would hide that.

regulation_scope.rule: The EU AI Act role terms are a FAILURE only in a row that is ABOUT the Regulation. Detected on the row's own text OR its English sibling naming the AI Act, the Regulation, 2024/1689, or an Article number. Elsewhere the same word is a FLAG.
regulation_scope.why: 42001 and 22989 have their own role vocabulary, and a 42001 role question is not wrong for using it. Gating the Regulation's terms across the whole catalogue would refuse correct work on the two certifications whose subject is a different standard -- the scope error this repository already paid for when a Scrum word list refused two ISO/IEC 42001 items.

aims_acronym.note: The AI management system's acronym. Spelling it out is always allowed in either language.

terms.note: SGSIA reads as SGSI, which is the ISMS -- a different management system, and on an ISO auditing certification that is a meaning error rather than a style one. Bare `AIMS` is allowed only as the certification code (AIMS-F, AIMS-IA), which the lint excludes by requiring a word boundary that is not a hyphen.
terms.autofix_note: SGSIA and SGia are one-to-one to SGIA. The bare English AIMS is 866 occurrences and is a POLICY backlog rather than a defect list -- reported, never auto-substituted, because a row may be glossing the English acronym on purpose.

iso_vocabulary_pt.note: ABNT conventions for ISO certifications in pt-BR.

terms.note: In an ISO certification a `standard` is a norma; `padrão` is a pattern or a benchmark. DOWNGRADED FROM failure TO flag ON ITS FIRST MEASUREMENT: it fires on 264 pt ISO rows, and `padrão` legitimately means `pattern` in AI content (`reconhecimento de padrões`). A gate on it would refuse correct work, and a guard that fires on the normal case is deleted by the first person it inconveniences. It becomes a failure when somebody has read the members.
terms.autofix_note: SENSE-DEPENDENT. padrao is both `standard` and `pattern`. Measured over the 264 ISO pt rows carrying it: 1 clearly the pattern sense, 15 clearly the standard sense, 248 not decidable by a crude probe. UNREAD, so flag only.

terms.note: Accreditation of a certification body is acreditação. `credenciamento` is a different administrative act.
terms.autofix_note: OFF. `credenciamento` -> `acreditação` is one-to-one, but `credenciada` is an adjective against a noun house form and would produce `entidade acreditação`. Two occurrences corpus-wide; a manual list is cheaper than a rule that has to know part of speech.

terms.note: Checked RELATIVE TO THE ENGLISH by the modal rule below, never as a word list: a pt row containing `deve` is only wrong if its English sentence carries no `shall`. AND THE ENGLISH WORD IS OFTEN THE SUBJECT OF THE ITEM -- `as declaracoes 'should' da ISO 19011 ... mais fracas do que 'shall'` is an item ABOUT the two modals, where leaving them in English is required and translating them would destroy the question. The untranslated check is therefore OFF for this term: it fired on 156 such rows.

ABNT renders `should` as `convém que`. `deveria` is flagged ONLY where the English sentence carries `should`, and only in an ISO certification -- a flag, not a failure, because the whole translated ISO corpus predates this ruling. Untranslated check OFF for the same reason as `shall`: the bare English modal is the object of study in the auditor certifications.

clause_reference_pt.note: One clause-reference word per row. The house form is seção / subseção.

terms.note: MIXING is the finding, not any single word. `cláusula` is the dominant form in the item bank (14,837 occurrences against 142) and `apartado`/`seção` dominate the lessons, and the 2026-09-20 census established that rewriting the majority to match the minority is not a consistency fix. So the corpus-wide word is NOT changed here; what is reported is a single ROW that uses two of these words for the same thing.
terms.autofix_note: The corpus word is deliberately NOT imposed; only a row mixing two is reported.

terms.note: THE PORTUGUESE FORM IS NOT VERIFIED. The ABNT NBR ISO 19011 edition is not on disk, so `apresentação justa` is the house form and NOT an official rendering. It is a FLAG and the lint says so: asserting an official term we do not hold is the defect the Scrum section of this ruling exists to avoid.
terms.autofix_note: The pt form is unverified against ABNT, so it is never written by a machine.

scrum_2020.blocked: The official 2020 Spanish and Portuguese Scrum Guides are NOT ON DISK. Only reference/scrum-guide-2020.pdf (English) is held. The ruling says to take the official terms from those editions and forbids reconstructing them from memory, so this family carries NO terms and the lint checks none of them. The terms needed are listed in SCRUM-GLOSSARY-NEEDED.md.

ruled_without_the_guides.first_use_carries_the_english: e.g. Objetivo del Sprint (Sprint Goal), Definição de Pronto (Definition of Done)

terms.census: house Scrum Team es 1047 / pt 1023; departures es 49, pt 75 -- 4 to 7 percent
terms.note: A minority form against a clear house convention, in both languages. FLAG rather than failure because 75 pt-BR occurrences of Equipe/Time Scrum are a real editorial choice somebody made repeatedly, not a slip, and the official guide keeps Scrum Team in English in both editions.

Spanish only. pt-BR is 1504 Developers against 1354 Desenvolvedores, which is a SPLIT CORPUS and not a convention with exceptions -- gating it would refuse 47 percent of the rows. The two languages genuinely differ here and the entry says so rather than averaging them.

terms.subject: scrum
terms.note: The 2020 Guide RETIRED `Development Team` as a role: the Scrum Team has no sub-team. This is the one entry that is a FAILURE rather than a flag, because it is not a register choice -- an item using it is testing a role that the current Guide does not contain. Eight occurrences, so the firing count is stated and small. Not auto-fixed: `Time de Desenvolvimento` sometimes appears inside a distractor that is wrong ON PURPOSE, and only a read can tell those apart.

scrum_2020.source: Scrum Guide 2020, official es-419 and pt-BR editions in reference/, read 2026-09-28
scrum_2020.house_form_note: RULED 2026-09-28: THE ENGLISH TERMS ARE THE HOUSE CONVENTION AND THEY STAY. Measured over 6,847 translated rows, our corpus keeps the Scrum artifacts and events in English -- Sprint Goal 1780 in es-419 against the official Objetivo del Sprint 9; Definition of Done 1934 against Definicion de Terminado 0; in pt-BR, Meta da Sprint 0 and Definicao de Pronto 2. The official 2020 editions translate those three and keep the roles and events in English. WE KEEP ALL OF THEM IN ENGLISH, deliberately. No bulk rewrite. The official forms are ALLOWED as a parenthetical gloss on first use -- see `allowed_glosses` -- and are never required and never substituted for the house term.
scrum_2020.gender_note: `Sprint` takes OPPOSITE genders in the two official guides and neither is unanimous: el sprint 64 / la sprint 17 in es-419, a sprint 71 / o sprint 15 in pt-BR. A gender rule would fire on the official translation itself, so there is none.

allowed_glosses.note: A gloss is the official term in PARENTHESES immediately after the house term, on FIRST USE in a lesson: `Sprint Goal (Objetivo del Sprint)`. It is an allowance, not an obligation, and it is never a substitution. The lessons where each term first appears are enumerated in SCRUM-GLOSS-FIRST-USE.md so the gloss can be added at the right place.
allowed_glosses.source: Scrum Guide 2020, official es-419 and pt-BR editions, reference/

iso_22989_roles.note: ISO/IEC 22989:2022 clause 5.19 stakeholder roles, added PROMPT-94 s3 when four family-level 5.19 entries were promoted to PRIMARY on AIMS-F task 1.2. An item anchored in 22989 must use its role names exactly, so the names are pinned before any 1.2 item is translated. EVERY FORM BELOW WAS COUNTED IN THE CORPUS by scripts/census-22989-role-terms.mjs; none was chosen.
iso_22989_roles.severity_rule: failure where one form is UNANIMOUS (no competing form attested) and appears at least 10 times; flag otherwise. A failure blocks a row, and blocking on a term seen twice would be a rule built on two observations.

provider_is_absent_deliberately.why: The eu_ai_act family says pt `prestador` and FORBIDS `fornecedor`. The corpus renders 22989's AI provider as `fornecedor de IA` 65 times, `provedor de IA` 21, and `prestador de IA` ZERO. Both families scope AIMS-F, so an entry here would put two families in contradiction about one word.
provider_is_absent_deliberately.contained_today: `regulation_scoped` in eu_ai_act downgrades `fornecedor` to a FLAG in a row that is not about the Regulation. 983 lint findings mention it; none is a failure. Nothing is broken.
provider_is_absent_deliberately.open_decision: Does 22989's AI provider render as `fornecedor de IA` (the corpus, 65) or `prestador de IA` (eu_ai_act's expected, 0 occurrences)? Director's call. Until it is made, no 22989 entry claims the word, and `provider` keeps its single existing rule.

terms.note: Unanimous in both languages with no competing form attested.
terms.autofix_note: Not auto-fixable. A role name is the subject of the item it appears in, so a bulk substitution may only run over a read sample, with the non-role senses excluded by id.

es: fabricante de IA -- a manufacturer. 22989's producer DESIGNS, DEVELOPS, TESTS AND DEPLOYS; manufacture is not the relation.
pt: fabricante de IA -- same: a manufacturer, not a producer in 22989's sense.
criador de IA -- a creator, which collapses the producer role into authorship.

terms.forbidden_note: PREVENTIVE, not corrective. A quiet lint here is NOT evidence the rule worked.

unattested_and_therefore_absent.why: Portuguese has no attested form at all, so there is nothing to pin. An invented `desenvolvedor de IA` would be a rule the corpus has never followed -- and 22989's AI developer is a SUB-ROLE that stayed supporting, so no key anchors on it either.

enforceability.note: The lint's only detection mechanism is the per-term `forbidden` list. A term with an empty one is read on every row and can produce no finding. The first version of this family had empty lists throughout, so it could not fire at all, and its own control caught that on the first run.
enforceability.firing_count_note: Zero, and expected to be zero: no competing form is attested anywhere in 6.5M characters of es-419 or 6.2M of pt-BR. The controls in translation-term-lint.mjs are what prove the enforceable terms CAN fire.
